questions.knowledge_point: Solving a 2x2 System of Equations Using an Inverse Matrix
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ 5 & 2\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 2-5\cdot 4}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{18}[\begin{aligned}2 & -4 \\ -5 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}7 \\ -3\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}4x-y=17 \\ x+4y=-17\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}17 \\ -17\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}4 & -1 \\ 1 & 4\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{4\cdot 4-(-1)\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{17}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{17}[\begin{aligned}4 & 1 \\ -1 & 4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}17 \\ -17\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
{\begin{aligned}x-2y=1 \\ 2x+2y=-1\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix 
$A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -2 \\ 2 & 2\end{aligned}].$
This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{1\cdot 2-(-2)\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now represent the solution to this system, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{6}[\begin{aligned}2 & 2 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5=2x-3y \\ 4x=y-2\end{aligned}\end{aligned}

questions.worked_solution:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ 4x-y=-2.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 \\ 4 & -1\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{2\cdot (-1)-4\cdot (-3)}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{10}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 3 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 \\ -2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}2y=x+3 \\ 7-y=-x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}-x+2y=3 \\ x-y=-7.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 2 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{(-1)\cdot (-1)-1\cdot 2}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{-1}[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 \\ -1 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}3 \\ -7\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Which of the following represents the solution to the system of linear equations given below?

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5x=1-3y \\ 3-4y=2x\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}5x+3y=1 \\ -2x-4y=-3.\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $Ax=b:$

$$
[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}5 & 3 \\ -2 & -4\end{aligned}].$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{5\cdot (-4)-(-2)\cdot 3}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}] \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system as:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =-\frac{1}{14}[\begin{aligned}-4 & -3 \\ 2 & 5\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Find a solution to the system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x+y=2 \\ 4x+3y=6.\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
This system can be written as

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052845/assets/843dcd4359e4b61eb9715966fbbe6c26363ab5cfc57c55f94b6a41a73ec7feb1.png)

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052845/assets/b9ba240f93ee3ec8c02e9718d62342dca0e0855e24c7b34ed97758a6eb7c46b8.png) This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{A}^{-1} & =\frac{1}{3\cdot 2-4\cdot 1}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

We can now find the solution to this system:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={A}^{-1}b \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 \\ -4 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 6\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 4\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

So the solution is $x=0$ and $y=2.$

canonical_examples.worked_solution:
First, we reorganize the equations so that they are in the right order, to get

$$
{\begin{aligned}2x-3y=5 \\ -5x+6y=-8.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can represent this system of equations in the form $A\mathbf{x} =\mathbf{b}\mathbin{:}$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052845/assets/240a1d2f7f93ec808127c9fa1791a77a43fcd7c0c84505540acc81c8b9fbc6e1.png)

To find the solution, we need to calculate the inverse of the coefficient matrix ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14052845/assets/7850cbafc78f2cf2ce14ae7111064bf2f5a029f4d1b97b6d5ebfc09e7126f44e.png) This gives

$$
